children: New Zealand's economy grew more slowly in the second quarter as the crisis in the Middle East weighed on the economy.

Official data out on Thursday showed gross domestic product (GDP) rose 0.2% in the second quarter on the prior quarter, better than analysts' forecast of a rise of 0.1% and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's forecast of no growth.
Annual GDP increased 2.6%, Statistics New Zealand data showed. The market had expected 2.2% increase.
"The 0.2 percent growth in economic activity in the June 2026 quarter reflects mixed results, with increases in nine out of 16 industries," Statistics New Zealand spokesperson Jason Attewell said.
The data showed that construction was the largest upward contributor to the overall increase in GDP, up 2.7% in the quarter.

After a prolonged period of weakness, New Zealand’s economy has begun to show signs of recovery, though growth was expected to come under pressure in the second quarter as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran drove up oil prices and fuelled uncertainty.

New Zealand's central bank said it expected the economic recovery to strengthen and become more broad-based, after raising the official cash rate earlier this month by 25 basis points for a second consecutive meeting to 2.75% as inflation remained above its target range.
With no clear winner emerging ahead of New Zealand's November 7 election, the economy has become a central battleground.

The ruling coalition was elected three years ago on a pledge to revive growth, while the opposition Labour Party is campaigning on measures to ease cost-of-living pressures on middle-income households.
Statistics New Zealand added the largest downward contributors to GDP in the June 2026 quarter were transport, postal and warehousing.
